title: Think Different — Here's to the crazy ones
festival: Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity
caseSummary: In 1997, Apple was 90 days from bankruptcy. The brand had lost its narrative and its premium price position. TBWA\Chiat\Day's Think Different was launched with a single 60-second spot voiced by Richard Dreyfuss, followed by 17 print posters featuring historical figures (Einstein, MLK, Picasso, Lennon-Ono, Gandhi, Earhart, Hitchcock, etc.) and a POS rollout across 8,000 authorized retailers worldwide. The campaign ran continuously for 5 years and is widely credited with restoring Apple's brand premium ahead of the iMac launch.
juryRationale: Awarded Gold in Film 1998 for the rare achievement of a brand manifesto that doesn't show the product. The jury cited the operation's restraint, the calibrated weight of each historical figure chosen, and the fact that — uniquely among brand-rescue campaigns — it succeeded in restoring the brand's premium price position without a single product demonstration. Tagline 'Think different.' is grammatically incorrect on purpose, a choice the jury called 'a masterclass in editorial discipline.'

performanceNotes.salesContext: Apple sold ~5M iMacs in the 12 months following the iMac launch (May 1998), a record for the brand at the time. The iMac launched 18 months into the Think Different rollout.
performanceNotes.brandPositionImpact: Apple share price recovered from $13/share at Think Different launch (Sept 1997) to $35/share by end of 1998. Market cap roughly tripled.
performanceNotes.culturalImpact: Cited as inflection point in 47+ academic marketing analyses. Phrase 'Think different' entered popular usage and was added to Merriam-Webster in 2014.
performanceNotes.longevity: Campaign ran continuously from 1997 to 2002 (5 years). Tagline 'Think different.' was active brand wordmark from 1997 to 2002, retained as legacy mark afterward.
performanceNotes.imitation: 47+ documented direct imitators in the brand-manifesto pattern since 1998 (Adidas Impossible Is Nothing, Honda Impossible Dream, Dove Real Beauty, Patagonia anti-claims, etc.).
